subject: Maths
title: Angles in triangles and quadrilaterals
subtitle: Angles · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can find missing angles in triangles and quadrilaterals using angle sum facts.

key_vocab.definition: The angles in a triangle always add up to 180°. The angles in a quadrilateral always add up to 360°.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can find missing angles in triangles and quadrilaterals using angle sum facts.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: triangle -- The angles in a triangle always add up to 180°. The angles in a quadrilateral always add up to 360°.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Triangle = 180°. Quadrilateral = 360°. Subtract known angles to find the missing one.
a + b + c = 180° (triangle)
Sum of angles in a triangle

Key examples:
  ✓ Triangle angles sum to 180°  (always)
  ✓ Quadrilateral angles sum to 360°  (always)
  ✓ Isosceles: two angles are equal  (base angles)
  ✗ Triangle angles sum to 360°  (that is a quadrilateral)
  ✗ All triangles have a right angle  (only right-angled ones)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – triangle missing angle
  A triangle has angles 50° and 70°. Find the third angle.
  Angles sum to 180°
  50 + 70 = 120
  180 − 120 = 60°
  = 60°
  (Always subtract the sum of known angles from 180°.)

Example 2 – isosceles triangle
  An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40°. Find the base angles.
  Base angles are equal; call them x
  40 + x + x = 180 → 40 + 2x = 180
  2x = 140 → x = 70°
  = 70° each
  (In isosceles triangles, the two base angles are always equal.)

sections.title: Algebraic angles
sections.content:
Form and solve an equation.

(a) Triangle: x, x, x + 60
(b) Triangle: 2x, 3x, 4x
(c) Quadrilateral: x, 2x, 3x, 4x
(d) Triangle: x + 10, 2x, x + 30

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Find the missing angle(s).

(a) Right-angled triangle: 90°, 35°, ?
(b) Equilateral triangle: all angles?
(c) Parallelogram: one angle is 70°; find all
(d) Kite: 100°, 60°, 100°, ?
(e) Triangle: 2x − 10, x + 20, x + 30; find x

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Angles in a triangle sum to 180°
✗ Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 180°
✓ An isosceles triangle has two equal angles
✗ An equilateral triangle has angles of 90°
✓ A right angle is exactly 90°
